justification: Standard: a new read-only script that sweeps every table pointing at a rule by id. Not Minor: it is the check a publish is now supposed to pass before it is called done. Not Critical: it writes nothing, opens a read-only connection, builds SQL only from names read from the catalogue after an identifier check, and is not wired into the ledger or CI so it cannot block anything.

pre_impl.existing_data: After Waverley's 4,446-rule publish on 2026-11-23 the sweep found 490 of 490 Waverley project_brief_rows, 32 da_responses rows and 2 setback controls pointing at superseded rules; 5 columns hold text ids. 32 id-referencing columns exist (foreign keys to regulatory_provisions plus columns named like a rule id).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I treated the publish as done once the rule proofs ran. A publish supersedes rules and creates new ids, and nothing in the commit script lists the tables that point at the old ids; only OC-24 noticed, and only for the brief.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: plan_brief_checks.brief_integrity counts stale pointers for one table; this sweeps all of them by catalogue. Text-id columns are joined on the text form instead of being skipped. The ledger's rule that every check script must be run by something is satisfied by an explicit allow-list entry with its mechanism (run by hand after every publish, needs a live database that CI lacks), not by wiring it as a gate that would be red today.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A column that cannot be checked is reported as NOT CHECKED and fails the run; it is never read as clean.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A council is called republished while the brief, saved responses or controls still cite superseded rules. The check names every such table with its count.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_check_provision_dependents.py -q ; python scripts/check_provision_dependents.py --council waverley
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A dead pointer in a live table does not fail, a history table fails, an unchecked column reads as clean, or a text-id column is joined as an integer.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Four deliberate breaks (dead pointer ignored, history tables failing, an error counted clean, text join dropped) each failed at least one test.
falsifiable_check.observed_green: 15 tests pass plus one real-layer test. Run for Waverley it reports exactly 3 live tables with dead pointers (project_brief_rows 490 of 490, da_responses 32 of 32, dcp_setback_controls 2 of 29), 0 unchecked columns, and exits 1; an unknown council slug exits 2 with nothing checked.

functions.name: verdict
functions.input: the per-column counts of rows and dead pointers
functions.output: pass or fail with one line per problem column
functions.if_none: a column with an error fails the run and is never read as clean

functions.name: sweep
functions.input: a read-only connection and an optional council slug
functions.output: rows, dead pointers and any error for every id column
functions.if_none: a failing column becomes an error row and the sweep carries on

functions.name: join_on
functions.input: a quoted column name and its data type
functions.output: the join text for that column
functions.if_none: any type other than an integer type joins on the text form

values.read_at: a left join of each id column to regulatory_provisions where the rule is not current
values.if_missing: an unreadable column is NOT CHECKED and fails

queries.purpose: Count rows and dead pointers for one id column of one council
queries.where_clause: join to regulatory_provisions on the id, counting rows whose rule is not current and, when a council is given, whose source_council matches; read-only connection, 60 s limit
catalogue queries on pg_constraint and information_schema for public tables only

break_it.scenario: A table keeps rule ids as text.
break_it.what_happens: An integer join would fail and the table would be skipped or read as clean.
break_it.how: Non-integer columns join on the text form and are counted.

break_it.scenario: A table is a backup or history table.
break_it.what_happens: It would fail every run for pointing at old rows on purpose.
break_it.how: Backup, change log, versions and archived tables are shown but do not fail.

break_it.scenario: A catalogue name contains a quote or a space.
break_it.how: Names must match a plain identifier pattern or the run raises before any query.

break_it.what_happens: It would be silently left out and the council called clean.
break_it.how: It is reported as NOT CHECKED, fails the run, and the sweep continues.

break_it.scenario: The list of id columns misses a table that points at rules, for example a new table with an unusual column name.
break_it.what_happens: That table would not be swept and the council could be called clean.
break_it.how: Every foreign key to regulatory_provisions is found by the catalogue whatever the column is called, plus the named id columns; a table with neither is listed in the plan as a known limit.

break_it.what_happens: Every count would be zero and the run would read as clean.
break_it.how: A council with no rules is refused with exit 2 before anything is swept.

break_it.scenario: A row points at a rule id that no longer exists or never did.
break_it.what_happens: It would not match a superseded rule and would be ignored.
break_it.how: An all-council run counts it as dead; a council run lists it as a note because it cannot be given a council.

break_it.scenario: A rule's current flag is null.
break_it.what_happens: The comparison would be unknown and the row would not be counted.
break_it.how: The test is IS NOT TRUE, so a null flag counts as not current.

post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/check_provision_dependents.py --council <name> after every council publish; the plan is ~/.claude/plans/ce-after-a-publish-dependents-PLAN-2026-11-23.md.
